observations: A blocky, roughly square form dominates the center against a dark blue-grey ground; its surface is built from stacked, rounded rectangular compartments outlined in dark lines and filled with deep purples and blacks.

Three eye-like forms appear across the upper half: two forward-facing ovals on the left with looping scribbles inside them, and one larger almond shape on the right filled with white, red, and a dark iris, tilted at an angle.

A horizontal band near the bottom holds a row of rounded tooth shapes in white and grey, framed by red and black lines; loose multicolored lines—pink, yellow, blue, red—escape the main form at the top and sides.
reading: The image presents a dense, block-like form whose compartments read as face parts—eyes, a mouth—yet the whole sits closer to a carved or assembled object than a living face. Looping scribbles inside each eye socket push against their containers, while the large tilted eye on the right sits apart, cooler and more open. The pale tooth row anchors the lower register, its rounded shapes neither smiling nor snarling but held in suspension.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #111 and #113. Where #111 fills its field with hot purples and reds and #113 strips back to smooth curves on grey, #112 is dark and dense but shot through with the same loose color lines seen across the subset.

connections.reason: Both works use layered looping scribbles inside eye sockets and expose rows of teeth, but #111 spreads across a hot magenta field while #112 compresses the same elements into a darker, boxier structure.

rawblocks #53 shares the dark blue-grey ground and the contrast of a dense, scribble-filled face form against open shadow, a pairing the collector links to the visual qualities connecting scrimshaw and nnxyz.

lookingQuestion: The large almond-shaped eye on the right is tilted and set apart from the two forward-facing sockets on the left—what does that asymmetry do to how you read the whole form?
ambiguities: The title-derived order and the recorded-creation order align here, but gaps exist elsewhere in the owned subset, so adjacency does not confirm sequential making.
The compartmented structure could be read as a mask, a carved object, or a face seen straight on; the image does not resolve which.
